title: `external-secrets.io/v1alpha1` removed (with the conversion webhook)

detection.reason: read from each object's managedFields: the apiVersion every field manager (kubectl, Helm, Argo CD, Flux) last wrote it with — the manifests that will fail to apply

quote: Removal of Conversion Webhooks and `SecretStore/v1alpha1`, `ExternalSecret/v1alpha1` and their cluster counterparts
remediation: Rewrite the manifests of the objects named in `external-secrets.io/v1` (v1alpha1 `dataFrom` entries become `dataFrom[].extract`) and re-apply them BEFORE the upgrade; 0.16 drops v1alpha1 and the conversion webhook, so an apply in v1alpha1 is refused.
verifyCommand: kubectl get externalsecrets.external-secrets.io,clusterexternalsecrets.external-secrets.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.metadata.managedFields[]?; .apiVersion == "external-secrets.io/v1alpha1")) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row was last written as v1alpha1 by some manager
coversNotes: v0.16.0: warning it is known v0.16.0 will not be an easy upgrade if you're not consuming from ou
v0.16.0: Make sure you are not using any v1alpha1 resources across all of your infrastructure.
v0.16.1: Make sure you are not using any v1alpha1 resources across all of your infrastructure.
CRD clustersecretstores.external-secrets.io: version v1alpha1 removed
CRD externalsecrets.external-secrets.io: version v1alpha1 removed
CRD secretstores.external-secrets.io: version v1alpha1 removed

title: CRD `status.storedVersions` still lists v1alpha1 — the 0.16 CRDs cannot be applied
quote: If that command returns not safe, remove v1alpha1 from your stored versions. Make sure this status is persisted after you verify these commands.
remediation: For each CRD named, migrate stored objects off v1alpha1 (re-write each object), then patch `status.storedVersions` to `["v1", "v1beta1"]` as the 0.16 upgrade guide shows; the 0.16 CRD drops v1alpha1 from spec.versions and the API server refuses that while it is still a stored version.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd externalsecrets.external-secrets.io secretstores.external-secrets.io clustersecretstores.external-secrets.io clusterexternalsecrets.external-secrets.io -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.storedVersions | index("v1alpha1")) | .metadata.name'  # each name still stores v1alpha1
coversNotes: v0.16.0: Make sure there are no storedVersions on v1alpha1 for externalsecrets clusterexternalse
v0.16.1: Make sure there are no storedVersions on v1alpha1 for externalsecrets clusterexternalse

title: 0.16 CRDs must be installed before the controller (conversion webhook removed)

detection.reason: how the CRDs are installed (Helm `installCRDs`, a separate bundle, Argo CD / Flux) is not collected; the CRDs themselves are

quote: If CRDs are installed separately, the first step you need to do is bump the crds:
remediation: Helm with `installCRDs=true` (the default) upgrades both. If the CRDs are applied separately, apply the 0.16.1+ bundle first, check it applies cleanly, then upgrade the controller — and use 0.16.1, never 0.16.0 (its CRDs still carried `spec.conversion.webhookClientConfig`). A failed CRD step shows up as `conversion webhook for external-secrets.io/v1, Kind=ExternalSecret failed`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group == "external-secrets.io") | "\(.metadata.name) conversion=\(.spec.conversion.strategy) helm=\(.metadata.labels["app.kubernetes.io/managed-by"] // "-")"'  # each row is an ESO CRD; Webhook conversion means the old CRD is still installed
coversNotes: v0.16.0: CRDs as part of external-secrets installation
v0.16.1: CRDs as part of external-secrets installation
v0.16.1: CRDs installed separately
v0.16.0: conversion webhook for external-secrets.io/v1 Kind ExternalSecret failed the server cou
v0.16.1: conversion webhook for external-secrets.io/v1 Kind ExternalSecret failed the server cou
v0.16.0: spec.conversion.webhookClientConfig Forbidden should not be set when strategy is not se
v0.16.1 (What's Changed): fix: remove crds from bundle
v0.16.1 (What's Changed): fix: remove the conversion hook completely
chart value crds.conversion.enabled default changed true -> false

title: Templating engine v1 removed

detection.reason: the agent writes templateEngineVersion on every ExternalSecret ("" when there is no template)

remediation: Port each template named to engine v2 (`engineVersion: v2`, Go templates with sprig; v1 helpers such as `pemCertificate` / `pemPrivateKey` become `filterPEM`), following upstream's templating-v1 migration guide, before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get externalsecrets.external-secrets.io,clusterexternalsecrets.external-secrets.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.target.template.engineVersion // .spec.externalSecretSpec.target.template.engineVersion // "") == "v1") | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row still renders with engine v1
coversNotes: ExternalSecret spec.target.template.engineVersion value v1 removed

title: Storage version moved to v1 — objects stored as v1beta1 stay so until rewritten
quote: Promotion of `ExternalSecret/v1` and `SecretStore/v1` and their cluster counterparts
remediation: Nothing breaks in 2.14 (v1beta1 is still listed, unserved). Before a future release drops v1beta1 from the CRDs, run a storage migration (rewrite every object) and trim `status.storedVersions` to `["v1"]` on the CRDs named.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group == "external-secrets.io") | select(.status.storedVersions | index("v1beta1")) | .metadata.name'  # each name still records v1beta1 as a stored version
coversNotes: CRD clusterexternalsecrets.external-secrets.io: storage version moved v1beta1 -> v1
CRD clustersecretstores.external-secrets.io: storage version moved v1beta1 -> v1
CRD externalsecrets.external-secrets.io: storage version moved v1beta1 -> v1
CRD secretstores.external-secrets.io: storage version moved v1beta1 -> v1

title: Fake provider `valueMap` removed

detection.reason: the fake provider's data[] entries are not in the store projection beyond their key names

quote: Removal of `ValueMaps` from Fake Secret Store
remediation: Replace `valueMap` with `value` in each fake store's `data[]` entry.
verifyCommand: kubectl get secretstores.external-secrets.io,clustersecretstores.external-secrets.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.provider | has("fake")) | select(any(.spec.provider.fake.data[]?; has("valueMap"))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a fake store still using valueMap

title: 0.16.2: generators with `refreshInterval: 0` or a no-refresh policy are re-generated

detection.reason: the projection carries each ExternalSecret's generator kinds and refresh settings separately; the pair is checked by the verify command

quote: When updating to `v0.16.2`, if you leverage `Generators` with `refreshInterval: 0` or any refreshPolicy to not update it, this version WILL FORCE THAT VALUE TO BE UPDATED.
remediation: Before moving past 0.16.1, back up the current values of every generator-backed Secret named whose ExternalSecret has `refreshInterval: 0` or a `refreshPolicy` other than Periodic (generated passwords, tokens); 0.16.2 regenerates them once. Restore or re-distribute the values after the upgrade.
verifyCommand: kubectl get externalsecrets.external-secrets.io,clusterexternalsecrets.external-secrets.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | (.spec // {}) as $s | ($s.externalSecretSpec // $s) as $e | select([($e.dataFrom // [])[]?.sourceRef.generatorRef] | map(select(. != null)) | length != 0) | select(($e.refreshInterval // "1h") == "0" or ($e.refreshInterval // "") == "0s" or (($e.refreshPolicy // "Periodic") != "Periodic")) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a generator-backed secret that 0.16.2 regenerates

title: AWS Secrets Manager PushSecret: metadata must use the `PushSecretMetadata` wrapper

detection.reason: which provider a PushSecret's store uses is a reference; the PushSecret projection carries the metadata FORMAT of each entry

remediation: For each PushSecret named that pushes to AWS Secrets Manager, rewrite `spec.data[].metadata` from the bare form (e.g. `{secretPushFormat: string}`, the 0.15 documented shape) to `apiVersion: kubernetes.external-secrets.io/v1alpha1`, `kind: PushSecretMetadata`, `spec: {secretPushFormat, tags, …}` before upgrading. From 0.16 the provider parses metadata strictly (#4538) and the bare form fails the push.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pushsecrets.external-secrets.io,clusterpushsecrets.external-secrets.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(any((.spec.data // .spec.pushSecretSpec.data // [])[]; .metadata != null and .metadata.kind != "PushSecretMetadata")) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name) stores=\([(.spec.secretStoreRefs // .spec.pushSecretSpec.secretStoreRefs // [])[].name] | join(","))"'  # each row pushes metadata without the PushSecretMetadata wrapper; check whether its store is AWS Secrets Manager
